changes: One aligned 48-byte device result allocation with existing typed argument views.
One persistent pinned 48-byte host result allocation; one result readback per batch.
Reuse one CUDA event pair per non-reentrant backend.
Remove redundant end-event synchronize; blocking copy on the same stream proves launch completion.
Reject invalid found flag; preserve independent hashlib proof/range/target validation.
selected_candidate.selection_reason: The pinned host candidate improved all five confirmation profiles in discovery and independent repetition; no geometry change was consistently faster.

measurement_conditions.other_known_gpu_jobs: No Hashcash GPU job, CUDA test or team benchmark ran concurrently; ordinary Windows desktop/browser graphics remained active.
measurement_conditions.cpu_policy: Other agents held heavy CPU benchmarking/build work until exclusive GPU window was released.
measurement_conditions.power_settings: Existing PC driver and power policy were preserved; no GPU clock lock, driver update or security-policy change.
measurement_conditions.warm_scope: Import/CUDA initialization, mandatory self-tests, kernel compile and warmup excluded from throughput; launch, flag reset, synchronization/copy, sample hash and independent proof checks included.
measurement_conditions.fixed_work_scope: Same UTF-8 message, target, nonce start, count, batch size and decimal length within each comparison; every hash completed even if a proof was found.
measurement_conditions.discovery_samples: 15 geometry screen candidates: 3 repetitions of 67,108,864 hashes; these exploratory ~20ms samples are explicitly below the 50ms confirmation threshold.
measurement_conditions.confirmation_samples: Geometry and pageable candidates: 9 repetitions; pinned discovery: 11; pinned independent confirmation: 13. Each confirmation sample processes 268,435,456 hashes in current production-size batches.
measurement_conditions.order: Forward and reverse variant execution order alternate by repetition.
measurement_conditions.variance: Every run, GPU event time, median, min/max, coefficient of variation, paired speedup and winner count retained. Desktop/WDDM overhead and boost clocks vary; medians do not guarantee each individual launch is faster.

host: Original independent buffers/new event pairs/serial result copies.
Shared device buffer/reused events/one pageable result copy/still explicit event synchronization.
Shared device buffer/reused events/persistent pinned host copy/no redundant event synchronization.

rejections.reason: Screen winner did not generalize: nine-repeat confirmation showed Korean difficulty5 0.988x and difficulty3 0.875x; retain original256×16.

rejections.candidate: Shared pageable host readback plus reused events
rejections.reason: Inconsistent: nine-repeat confirmation included Korean0.993x and difficulty7 0.956x; the pinned/no-double-sync refinement was then confirmed.

coverage: Mandatory digest and positive/negative search self-tests.
UTF-8 messages including33–35 bytes, padding and decimal boundaries.
Found proof then no proof then found proof on the same reused result buffer.
A real positive proof near UINT64_MAX validates both nonce words.
Independent hashlib verification of every benchmark returned proof and per-batch last hash.

limitations: These are warmed fixed-work throughput numbers, not end-to-end startup or guaranteed proof-discovery times.
Backend constructor self-tests and first-use compilation remain mandatory; no startup speedup is claimed from this evidence.
Actual proof search, CPU-only, CPU+GPU overlap, cancellation/restart and UI/history regression are separate coordinator-level gates.
Scope is this RTX5070Laptop/CuPy14.2/CUDA12.9 environment and the measured inputs. Other cards and workloads are unmeasured.
Persistent result/event buffers make the backend non-reentrant, as its original mutable result arrays already did.

geometry_screen.method: Identical UTF-8 input and contiguous finite nonce ranges; all hashes completed regardless of proof; compilation and runtime self-tests excluded; current production batch sizes unchanged; alternating execution order; event kernel time and complete backend wall time reported separately; each returned proof and per-batch last hash checked with independent hashlib SHA-256.
